comment: For skills, I look at it like this: a skill helps the LLM avoid reinventing the workflow every time. Instead of having to generate a process from scratch or interpret how a specific task should be handled, it can follow a predefined set of instructions, tools, and procedures designed for that workflow. The LLM is still involved, but less of the work is left to open-ended generation and reasoning. That can make the workflow faster and more consistent while reducing unnecessary token usage, compute, and other resources.
